record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Random Matrix Theory and the Theory of Integrable Systems. II
record.original_question: For the QR eigenvalue algorithm on random matrices, can one determine the bulk statistics of eigenvalue ratios near zero together with the associated eigenvector information well enough to prove a universality theorem analogous to the Toda result?

evidence.quote: It is very much an open problem to control, as n → ∞, the statistics of |λj+1/λj|, |λj−1/λj| for λj ∼ 0 deep in the bulk of the spectrum, together with their associated normalized eigenvectors, as in (8), (9).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M_n$ be an $n \times n$ random real symmetric (or Hermitian) matrix drawn from a Wigner-type ensemble, with eigenvalues $\lambda_1 \le \lambda_2 \le \cdots \le \lambda_n$ and corresponding normalized eigenvectors $v_1,\dots,v_n$. Consider the shifted QR eigenvalue algorithm applied to $M_n$, which produces an iteration $M_n^{(0)} = M_n, M_n^{(k+1)} = R_k Q_k + \sigma_k I$ where $M_n^{(k)} - \sigma_k I = Q_k R_k$ is the QR factorization and $\sigma_k$ is an appropriate shift. The convergence rate of the QR algorithm at step $k$ near an eigenvalue $\lambda_j$ deep in the bulk of the spectrum (i.e., $\lambda_j$ near $0$ for an ensemble whose limiting spectral density is supported around $0$) is governed by the ratios $|\lambda_{j+1}/\lambda_j|$ and $|\lambda_{j-1}/\lambda_j|$ together with overlap information from the eigenvectors $v_{j-1}, v_j, v_{j+1}$ with the canonical basis.

Problem: As $n \to \infty$, determine the joint limiting statistics of the ratios
$$\bigl(|\lambda_{j+1}/\lambda_j|,\ |\lambda_{j-1}/\lambda_j|\bigr)$$
for indices $j$ such that $\lambda_j$ lies deep in the bulk near $0$, together with the joint distribution of the relevant components of the associated normalized eigenvectors $v_{j-1}, v_j, v_{j+1}$, in sufficient detail to establish a universality theorem for the (suitably rescaled) running time / halting-time fluctuations of the shifted QR eigenvalue algorithm on $M_n$, analogous to the universality theorem known for the Toda algorithm on random matrices.
artifact.category_tag: Random matrix theory and numerical algorithms
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work by Deift, Trogdon and collaborators has established universality results for halting times of certain eigenvalue algorithms (power method, inverse power method, and the QR algorithm applied to sample covariance matrices for extreme eigenvalues), as well as for conjugate gradient and MINRES. However, controlling the bulk statistics of consecutive eigenvalue ratios $|\lambda_{j\pm 1}/\lambda_j|$ near zero together with the associated eigenvector information, in order to prove a Toda-like universality theorem for the bulk behaviour of the QR algorithm, does not appear to be settled in the literature found.

status_evidence.title: Universality for Eigenvalue Algorithms on Sample Covariance Matrices
status_evidence.snippet: Proved a universal limit theorem for the halting time of the power/inverse power methods and the QR eigenvalue algorithm for extreme eigenvalues of random sample covariance matrices.
status_evidence.claim: Universality is known for extreme-eigenvalue computations via QR on covariance matrices, not for ratios deep in the bulk.

status_evidence.title: Universality in numerical computations with random data
status_evidence.snippet: Empirical universal fluctuations are observed for widely used numerical algorithms applied to random data.
status_evidence.claim: Universality is observed empirically but bulk-ratio analysis for shifted QR remains incompletely proved.
